decisions.decision: Owning module is telemetry; one standalone change, not a roadmap
decisions.why: The analytics edits are forced signature updates with no analytics design decision. Same shape as the MAG-64 pilot.

decisions.decision: Election: prefer OWNER, else any candidate, tie broken by lowest account_id; never skip a car
decisions.why: User first chose skip-when-no-OWNER, then reversed once shown it permanently stops the DRIVER-only car Palomito Nachito.

decisions.decision: Election makes no token liveness check; stays pure Go
decisions.why: AccessTokenFor rotates the single-use refresh token, so probing candidates would rotate tokens for accounts that poll nothing.

decisions.decision: Design gate passed: no second index; only the index UNIQUE (tesla_id, captured_date) creates
decisions.why: Departs from the ticket's own bullet. Follows MAG-63's rule: justify every index against a query that exists today.

decisions.decision: Accepted the artifact worker's output although it died before sending its final report
decisions.why: Rate limit killed it after all four files were written. Leader verified them instead of paying a full re-dispatch.

decisions.decision: Migration file renumbered 20260911000001 -> 20260911000002; SQL content unchanged
decisions.why: design.md picked a version already used by the analytics pilot migration. make migration-guard failed and named the renumber as its own fix.

decisions.decision: Do not apply the migration to the dev database at any point in this change
decisions.why: Tests provision their own Postgres and apply migrations themselves. The Up migration DELETEs duplicate rows, and the dev DB holds snapshot history Tesla cannot backfill.

decisions.decision: Rewrote 7 query doc comments, not the 6 tasks.md names
decisions.why: SnapshotPrecedingDay also named the retired constraint. Leaving it would have left a stale name pointing at a dropped object.

decisions.decision: Deleted LatestSnapshotsByVehicles_DifferentAccountExcluded and SnapshotsByVehicleSince_CrossAccountExcluded; kept the third as SnapshotsByVehicleBetween_SiblingVehicleExcluded
decisions.why: Both deleted tests only proved the account filter this change removes, and the second had a fixture that collides on the new key. The third also proves sibling-vehicle exclusion, which stays valid.

decisions.decision: vehicle_metrics.account_id is now set from the caller accountID in recalculate.go, not from the snapshot
decisions.why: design.md missed this. The old telemetry query filtered by account, so the snapshot account always equalled the caller. Behaviour identical, no schema change, so no design gate.

decisions.decision: Renamed LatestSnapshotsByAccount in 6 comments across analytics and gateway; left the historic migration file untouched
decisions.why: A comment naming a deleted method misleads the next reader. Historic migrations are never edited.

decisions.decision: Swept all six docs naming LatestSnapshotsByAccount, including the two pre-existing gateway ones
decisions.why: Four were invalidated by this change. openspec/specs/gateway/spec.md was already wrong since RM38: the charges suggestion reads analytics, not telemetry.

decisions.decision: SnapshotPrecedingDay orders by captured_date DESC, not captured_at DESC
decisions.why: design.md D-INDEX claimed the (tesla_id, captured_date) index serves captured_at ordering. It does not. One row per day means the two orderings pick the same row, so no second index is needed.

decisions.decision: account_id is relaxed to NULLABLE, not dropped; the drop moves to a follow-up
decisions.why: Migrations run one module dir at a time, so a 2026-09-08 analytics backfill joining vs.account_id runs after our drop on a fresh database and fails. Filed as backlog 31.

decisions.decision: Leader bug: the wave-5 script deleted whole lines starting with AccountID:, taking TeslaID with them on 15 shared lines
decisions.why: Every analytics DB failure came from tesla_id 0: empty query results, duplicate-key collisions, no backfill match. Restored by diffing against the wave-4 file.

decisions.decision: Identity assertions move from account_id to tesla_id instead of being deleted
decisions.why: User asked for tesla_id rather than removal. FixtureA/B/C already assert TeslaID, and both scoping tests keep their supercharger and manual halves.

decisions.decision: SUPERSEDED by D18: seedSnapshot split for the TPMS migration test
decisions.why: The user deleted the test instead, so the split had no purpose and was reverted.

decisions.decision: Deleted TestMigration_TpmsPressureBackfill and its file; reverted the seedSnapshot split
decisions.why: User does not want migration tests. Coverage lost: proof that the 2026-09-08 TPMS backfill filled the columns. That migration already ran everywhere.

decisions.decision: Standing rule added to ai/go-conventions.md Testing: never write migration tests, delete them on sight; deleted the 3 remaining ones
decisions.why: Owner verifies migrations by checking the database directly. A migration is frozen but its fixture is not, so later schema changes break tests of work that already ran.

decisions.decision: Third raw-SQL fixture bug fixed: the recapture UPDATE still filtered on account_id; added a RowsAffected check
decisions.why: An UPDATE matching zero rows does not error, so the recapture silently never happened and the assertion failed for the wrong reason. My earlier line-based grep missed it because the SQL spans lines.
